newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdanski to lead $100 mln shipyard loan.
newsitem.headline: Gdanski to lead $100 mln shipyard loan.

text.p: Poland's Bank Gdanski said on Friday it had agreed to organise a consortium of banks which would lend the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard some $100 million to build five ships for a German shipowner.

However, Gdanski said that before it would start organising the loan the shipyard would have to present a sound restructuring plan guaranteeing that the work would be carried out according to an agreed schedule.
It also wants the German shipowner to give credit guarantees for a part of the loan and expects that trade unions would not disrupt production.

"Only after the shipyard produces that information and Bank Gdanski accepts it will it be possible to apply for government guarantees and begin organising the consortium of banks which will finance the building of the ships," the statement said.

The ships will be built by a company carved out of the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, called Nowa Stocznia Gdanska (New Gdansk Shipyard). The firm, now existing only on paper, is not burdened with its parent's debts which exceed 415 million zlotys.

Late on Thursday, the government confirmed it was ready to offer a partial guarantee for the loan, which would keep some of the yard's 4,800-strong workforce busy while an investor to save the whole business is sought.
